{{Short description|Algebraic surface}}
[[Image:Chatelet surface.png|thumb|right|300px|Some snapshots showing the real points of the Châtelet surface with ''P''(''x'') = ''x''<sup>3</sup> – 5''x''<sup>2</sup> – 6''x''. Axes: ''x'' = red, ''y'' = yellow, ''z'' = blue]]

In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Châtelet surface''' is a [[rational surface]] studied by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=François Châtelet (mathematician)|last=Châtelet|year=1959}} given by an equation

:<math>y^2-az^2=P(x), \, </math>

where ''P'' has degree 3 or 4.  They are [[conic bundle]]s.
